subject: Visibility request: per-route cost & latency breakdown for procurement
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Request: per-route cost/latency breakdown for procurement review

Hi Marissa,

Hope you're well — following up from our call today. Procurement at Acme asked for more concrete observability on usage economics before we finalize the reserved capacity commitment: specifically, they want a per-route breakdown of latency and cost so they can compare expected spend across different product surfaces (search, summarization, recommendations).

Key asks from their side:
- Time-series (daily/weekly) of p50/p95/p99 latency by route
- Cost per 1k tokens and total spend per route (rolling 30d)
- Ability to filter by model/version and region
- Sample of raw request/response timing histogram (for 1 route)

I attached the procurement requirements doc that lists fields they'd like to see. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can produce these exports or dashboards (even as CSV exports) within a two-week window?

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
Senior PM, Integrations
Acme Retail

- acme_req_2026.pdf (PDF)

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement ask. High level: they need per-route observability (latency percentiles and cost breakdown) with filtering by model/version and region. Procurement wants something they can attach to their SOW decision in ~2 weeks.

Checklist of what I think matters (please update/replace):
- Exports: daily time-series for p50/p95/p99 latency for each public route (and any customer-named routes), rolling 30d cost per route, total spend per route.
- UI: per-route dashboard with time-range selector and model/version filter (stretch goal).
- Alerting: ability to set alerts on P95 latency spikes or cost burn rate for a route.
- Data retention: procurement expects 12 months of historical summary (not necessarily raw traces).

Questions for engineering/product:
1) What data do we already collect that's route-attributed vs. what needs tagging?
2) Can we generate on-demand CSV exports for a customer-scoped set of routes?
3) Estimated effort: quick export (1-2 days), small dashboard (2-3 sprints), production-grade per-route dashboards with alerts (4+ sprints)?

Please respond with gaps and a recommended minimal deliverable by Feb 24 so I can update Acme. Attaching the procurement requirements and a quick mock (mock_screens_v2.png) that shows what they asked for visually.

—Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:26:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: per-route cost/latency breakdown for procurement review

Quick engineering assessment:

Summary: We have most of the raw telemetry (per-request timing, model used, route tag, region, token counts) in our tracing/metrics pipeline, but it's currently aggregated at the model+region level in long-term storage. Per-route breakdown exists transiently in our request logs (last 7 days in raw form).

Gaps & constraints:
- Cardinality: 'route' is a high-cardinality dimension. Full per-route long-term retention at raw granularity will increase storage and query cost significantly.
- Cost attribution: We compute cost at the model + token type level, not per-route; mapping from request -> cost requires joining request logs with billing granules (cheap but not precomputed).
- Real-time UI: Building an interactive per-route dashboard that supports arbitrary time ranges and percentiles will need pre-aggregation (daily/hourly) and a small UI component — estimated 4 weeks of focused work + infra for retention.

Proposed minimal deliverable (fast path):
1) On-demand CSV export: a job that joins logs + billing granules to produce daily p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-route for a customer-provided list of routes (rolling 30d). Implementation estimate: ~3 engineer-days and a job we can run per-customer.
2) Short-term dashboard mock: product builds a UI mock and we wire the CSV job as a backend to power it (no heavy pre-aggregation). Estimate: 1 sprint for UI + 1 week to wire with exports.

If procurement needs 12 months of historical summary, we can generate a summarized monthly rollup (not raw traces) as part of the CSV export — reasonable cost to produce for a purchase/renewal.

Risks: repeated export runs for many customers could strain the join job; consider quotas.

I'll open a spike ticket to prototype the join job and a sample export.

—Vivek
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: per-route cost/latency breakdown for procurement review

This looks reasonable. Product notes / priorities:
- Minimal deliverable = the on-demand CSV export + a templated dashboard (reads CSV) we can show to the customer. That should satisfy procurement immediacy and keep infra cost low.
- For the 12-month request: provide monthly rollups (p50/p95) and a cost summary; flag that percentiles on monthly rollups have lower fidelity.
- UI experience: we should include a route-tag selector, model/version filter, and a small "cost breakdown" panel that shows token vs infra costs.

I'll open the Jira (INF-4872) and create a short PRD with success criteria and the example screens (link in ticket). If the export job is ready, CS (Evelyn) can produce the CSV for Acme and we can run an internal sanity check before sending.

Timeline ask from sales: commit to a sample CSV by Feb 24. If engineering thinks the 3-day estimate is tight, tell me what you need and we'll negotiate a date with Acme.

—Lauren
Product Manager, Console & Observability

Product will prep a templated dashboard (reads the CSV) to demonstrate the experience.

We expect to produce a sample CSV for the routes you listed in the requirements doc by Feb 24. If procurement can accept the CSV + templated dashboard as the deliverable for the SOW, we can proceed on that cadence.

Next steps for Acme: please reply to confirm (A) the exact route names you want included in the sample, and (B) whether monthly rollups for 12 months are sufficient (we'll note fidelity limits).

Marissa Cole
